newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum stock draw destined for consumers-Spector.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum stock draw destined for consumers-Spector.

text.p: The aluminum being taken out of LME warehouses was destined for consumers and not merely being transferred to a 'stealth stockpile', industry analyst Stewart Spector said in his latest monthly review.
The slim forward month premium over cash aluminum price or contango on LME does not make it economic to handle and transport metal from one location to another, Spector said.
"Therefore we discount the constant talk about the transfer of LME warranted ingot to some "stealth stockpile" as an irrational rumor," Spector said.
Tuesday, LME aluminum stocks fell 975 tonnes to 670,850 tonnes.
Aluminum consumers have destocked and are seeing rising orders which needed more metal to fulfill.
"Thus, in our opinion, the metal moving out of the LME warehouses is for real," Spector said.

Nevertheless, the aluminum price has yet to reflect declining stocks because of three factors which have impeded it - unwarranted consignment inventory of ingot financed by the banks, the supposed large LME 'strangle' aluminum options position held by L G Metals Corp, and the fall in copper prices which dampened the base metals complex, Spector said.

It could take another month or so for the banks to unwind their mismatched forward positions, and the L G Metals aluminum positions have been turned over to a major investment banker to be worked out, Spector said.
"However, the sharp drop in copper and aluminum prices on heavy volume in the last week should have allowed the banker to have closed out those positions," Spector said.
